newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland able to finance 1.9 pct 1998 gap - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Poland able to finance 1.9 pct 1998 gap - analyst.

text.p: Poland should keep 1998's budget deficit at or below the planned 1.9 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) to avoid problems with its financing, the head of the state-funded Institute of Finance said on Friday.

"I believe that within the planned level of the deficit of 1.9 percent of GDP, it will be possible to finance it. But this is the absolute conceiveable maximum," Andrzej Wernik, director of the semi-independent institute told Reuters in an interview.
The Finance Ministry proposes to cut the deficit from 1997's planned 2.8 percent, accounting for financing restraints and aiming to cool domestic demand, which should tame the widening trade gap.
The central bank criticized the plan, saying a much deeper fiscal tightening was needed. It said a 1.5-percent gap was the highest acceptable level.
But Wernik said one should not overestimate the impact of such a cut on Poland's external position.
"Those concerned with the trade deficit have too much faith in fiscal tightening...budget expenditures are not generating high imports," he said.
"I am afraid that if we cut the deficit to 1.5 percent, or two billion zlotys ($605.3 million), this would not save our trade balance ...it is not such a simple relationship," he added.

Poland's trade deficit is expected to grow to $12 billion this year or about 5-6 percent of GDP. But the central bank has warned it could reach about 7-8 percent of GDP next year if Poland fails to tighten reins on booming investment and consumer demand to stem imports growth.
